tasks.short: Negotiate prices, delivery commitments and other sales terms with technical buyers.

steps.what: Review account history, quoted products, costs and current delivery constraints.
Calculate discount options, margin effects and permitted concessions.
Discuss trade-offs and negotiate provisional terms with the buyer.
Record provisional terms and explain any requested exceptions.
Approve exceptions beyond the representative's delegated commercial limits.
Send the approved terms to the buyer and update the opportunity.

tasks.design: A calculator combines account data from the {CRM}, costs and availability from the {ERP}, and approved concession rules. A structured form in the {CRM} routes exceptional terms through the {WORKFLOW}; approved terms produce a confirmation in the {EMAIL} after the representative checks it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cost, delivery and delegation data were separated. Maintaining the calculator and approval links took more effort than using a workbook.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing interfaces and faster AI-assisted coding reduce the effort of connecting records and implementing explicit concession rules.
tasks.still_hard: Buyer priorities, technical risk and bargaining power remain contextual. Delivery estimates and costs can change during negotiations.
tasks.human_edge: The representative reads hesitation, protects trust and trades concessions against commitments the buyer actually values.

ambition.what: Live margin checks for each proposed concession during negotiations

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to assembling facts and recalculating offers. The representative can evaluate concessions during the conversation within existing delegation limits; approval rights do not expand.

reach.task: Review a proposed discount against margin and account value.
reach.learn: Contribution margin, concession sequencing and commercial delegation.

reach.task: Assess whether a delivery or performance promise is technically supportable.
reach.learn: Application limits, implementation dependencies and technical escalation.

evidence.claim: Elfsquad links product configuration and quoting to ERP and CRM records.
Explicit price, margin and delegation rules can generate concession options without a model.
Negotiation usually retains substantial human conversation despite faster preparation.

assumptions: The company sells mainly to organisational buyers and maintains approved commercial delegation limits.
The time split covers preparation, conversation and paperwork; exception approval time is averaged across cases.
Terms within delegated limits bypass sales manager approval.
The proposed preparation and paperwork changes do not require an autonomous agent.
Build ranges assume one product family and existing interfaces. GDPR applies to buyer contact data.
unknowns: Whether current costs and credible delivery estimates are accessible.
Which concessions require commercial, finance or legal approval.
How often representatives use a workbook for concession calculations.
Whether the existing {CRM} supports structured terms and approvals.
research_questions: Which concession combinations can be expressed as explicit rules?
How stale can costs and availability be before a negotiation brief becomes misleading?
Do proposed activity logs require employee consultation under national rules?
new_work: Maintain price, margin and delegation rules.
Resolve stale or conflicting cost and delivery inputs.
Review exceptional concessions and maintain integration access.

tasks.short: Prepare sales contracts from approved terms and submit them for customer signature.

steps.what: Retrieve approved terms, the buyer order and verified customer details.
Populate the contract template with products, prices, delivery and approved clauses.
Compare the draft with buyer conditions and identify conflicting obligations.

loop.input: Contract draft, buyer conditions, approved sales terms and approved clause library.
loop.output: Clause deviation report with source passages and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Compare numeric fields deterministically. A person checks clause coverage, cited passages and proposed deviations against the documents.
loop.stop: At most two passes for documents up to 20 pages. Longer documents, missing passages or failed checks go to manual comparison.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text buyer conditions can change obligations without matching known clause wording. Template rules handle standard contracts.

steps.what: Resolve and approve nonstandard legal clauses before release.
Check the recipient and submit the approved contract for signature.
File the submitted version and link its status to the opportunity.

tasks.design: Approved terms from the {CRM} and order details from the {ERP} populate controlled templates in the {CLM}. A bounded clause comparison produces a review report, while legal exceptions receive human approval; the {ESIGN} sends the checked version and synchronises submission status to the {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates existed, but fields were copied between records and documents. Buyer wording made automatic clause comparison unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured templates and interface mappings handle standard contracts. A bounded model can highlight free-text deviations for review without deciding their acceptability.
tasks.still_hard: Liability, technical guarantees and conflicting buyer terms need legal judgement. Correct entity names, signing authority and version control remain essential.
tasks.human_edge: People decide which obligations the business can accept and explain disputed terms to the buyer.

ambition.what: A pre-signature obligation brief naming delivery, warranty and acceptance responsibilities

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time copying fields and more time clearing obligations before signature. Legal approval and signature authority remain as currently delegated.

reach.task: Check that a submitted contract contains usable order and delivery information.
reach.learn: Order completeness, product identifiers and release conditions.

reach.task: Assess the commercial effect of a nonstandard warranty or acceptance clause.
reach.learn: Contract risk, margin exposure and approval thresholds.

evidence.claim: Elfsquad supports configuration and quote preparation linked to ERP and CRM data.
Controlled templates can populate standard sales contracts from structured approved terms.
A bounded model can suggest clause deviations, but legal acceptance still requires human judgement.

assumptions: A controlled clause library and standard contract templates already exist.
The buyer order has been captured as structured order data before this task.
Standard contracts bypass legal exception approval when policy allows.
Submission does not itself authorise order release or prove customer acceptance.
Build ranges cover one template family and one signature workflow. GDPR applies to contact and signatory data.
unknowns: How often buyers impose their own terms.
Which clauses require legal or commercial approval.
Whether existing {CLM} and {ESIGN} interfaces support the required version and status links.
Who may submit and sign contracts for each legal entity.
research_questions: Can current template configuration eliminate custom contract generation code?
Does clause comparison find material deviations in historical contracts without excessive false alerts?
Which checks must block submission even for standard contracts?
new_work: Maintain approved clauses, templates and field mappings.
Review clause reports and handle documents outside the loop budget.
Check recipients, attachments and versions before submission.
Resolve failed signature requests and status synchronisation.
Retest comparisons when templates or buyer conditions change.

tasks.short: Visit customers to understand technical needs, demonstrate products and agree next actions.

steps.what: Review the account, previous visits, open opportunities and relevant product documents.
Agree the appointment, attendees, agenda and site access arrangements.
Travel to the customer's establishment.
Inspect the application, operating conditions and technical constraints with customer staff.
Discuss needs, demonstrate relevant products and agree possible next actions.
Write the visit report and update requirements and actions in the account.
Send the customer a recap and assign technical follow-up.

tasks.design: A job assembles a linked visit pack from the {CRM}, {ERP} and {DOCS}, while the {CALENDAR} supports appointment coordination. A mobile form in the {CRM} captures observations and agreed actions once; the {WORKFLOW} prepares a checked recap in the {EMAIL} and routes technical questions to the sales engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparation and follow-up were scattered across account screens, documents and correspondence. Mobile forms often did not match technical discovery needs.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing calendar and mobile record features can be configured. Faster coding makes assembling a useful visit pack and connecting follow-up practical.
tasks.still_hard: Travel, physical inspection and demonstrations still take time. Hidden operating constraints and conflicting customer priorities require conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The representative notices practical conditions, asks follow-up questions and builds confidence through a credible demonstration.

ambition.what: An application-fit review with a documented technical question list after each qualifying visit

tasks.altitude: Preparation and paperwork shrink, while most of the week still involves travel and customer visits. The representative can structure application-fit reviews within existing technical competence and escalate unresolved questions.

reach.task: Turn site observations into an application-fit assessment.
reach.learn: Required measurements, operating limits and evidence needed for technical validation.

reach.task: Plan a demonstration around the customer's operating conditions.
reach.learn: Demonstration design, safe handling and observable success criteria.

evidence.claim: Structured account data and document links can generate a visit pack without a model.
Mobile forms and workflow rules can reuse visit findings for records, recaps and technical handoffs.
Physical application assessment and relationship-building remain substantially human.

assumptions: The typical visit includes travel, technical discovery and some product discussion or demonstration.
The visit pack assembles existing records without generating a narrative summary.
Recaps use structured findings and approved wording; bespoke technical claims require personal handling.
Build ranges cover one visit form and one technical handoff. GDPR applies to contact details and visit records.
unknowns: Actual travel time and visit duration.
Which applications require specialist inspection or regulated qualifications.
Whether representatives can use mobile forms at customer sites.
Which site observations and photographs customers permit the company to retain.
research_questions: Which discovery fields make a technical follow-up usable without another customer visit?
Can existing mobile {CRM} features provide acceptable offline capture?
Would any proposed location or activity tracking require consultation under national rules?
new_work: Maintain visit-pack links and discovery forms.
Check recaps for unsupported promises before sending.
Handle missing site information and specialist referrals.
Keep technical handoff queues and document versions current.

tasks.short: Keep customer contacts, account details and sales activity records accurate in the customer system.

steps.what: Open the customer account and gather verified account changes and completed sales activities.
Check account identifiers, addresses and commercial fields against the finance customer master.
Enter validated details and link completed activities to the correct account.
Resolve duplicate contacts, ambiguous account links and conflicting details.
Request missing contact or account details from the customer.

tasks.design: Configured rules in the {CRM} collect structured updates and link completed sales activities, while an integration compares shared account fields with the {ERP}. Validated updates write automatically, conflicts enter a review queue, and an approved template in the {EMAIL} requests essential missing details through a form in the {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shared fields lacked clear ownership and consistent identifiers. Representatives compensated by comparing screens and entering the same information again.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record rules cover most updates. Faster integration development makes field ownership, validation and reliable synchronisation affordable.
tasks.still_hard: Subsidiaries, shared contacts and disputed account ownership create ambiguous matches. GDPR retention and access requirements must fit actual customer data use.
tasks.human_edge: The representative recognises relationship context and knows when apparently similar records represent different buyers or buying centres.

ambition.what: An account handover pack showing verified contacts, open commitments and unresolved data gaps

tasks.altitude: Routine account maintenance largely leaves the representative's week, leaving a small conflict queue and more customer-facing time. Account correction authority stays within existing permissions; finance-controlled fields remain with the finance team.

reach.task: Validate a new customer's identity and required account fields.
reach.learn: Entity identifiers, account hierarchies and required onboarding evidence.

reach.task: Resolve mismatched delivery and billing account details before order processing.
reach.learn: Customer master ownership, address validation and downstream order effects.

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-10; 10-30 if new employee monitoring requires consultation under national rules

evidence.claim: Structured customer record maintenance is commonly handled by configured record rules and integrations.
Explicit field ownership and stable account identifiers allow deterministic synchronisation without a model.
Ambiguous account merges need human judgement because errors can affect several downstream records.

assumptions: Most updates arrive as structured, verified data, consistent with the supplied prior.
Free-text account changes are redirected to a structured form or handled as exceptions.
The {ERP} owns finance-controlled customer fields; the {CRM} owns sales relationship fields.
Automatic external requests use approved factual templates, permitted recipients and frequency limits.
No new employee performance scoring is included. Build ranges cover one customer master connection.
unknowns: Which system owns each shared field.
Whether stable customer identifiers exist across the {CRM} and {ERP}.
The duplicate rate and proportion of changes arriving only in free text.
Applicable retention periods, access permissions and employee consultation arrangements.
Whether current activity capture would expand employee monitoring.
research_questions: Which native {CRM} rules already remove manual entry?
What match criteria safely distinguish legal entities, sites and buying centres?
Which changes require finance approval rather than a sales correction?
What consultation is required under applicable national rules before rollout?
new_work: Resolve ambiguous matches and approve account merges.
Maintain field ownership, validation and synchronisation rules.
Handle failed updates and bounced detail requests.
Review retention, access and deletion propagation.
Check that activity capture remains within its approved purpose.

role.altitude: The representative spends more time on technical discovery, customer relationships and negotiated commitments. Preparation, contract assembly and routine records shrink, while commercial and legal authority remain explicitly delegated.
reach: Support sales managers with live concession and margin analysis.
Give sales engineers structured application evidence and unresolved technical questions.
Give order clerks complete contract and customer information before order processing.
Help new accounts clerks distinguish entities, sites and buying centres.
skills_to_grow: Customer master data and account hierarchies
Reviewing generated artefacts and resolving exceptions
role.ambitious_version: Offer an application-fit review that connects site findings, approved commercial options and a pre-signature obligation brief. The representative leads the customer conversation, with sales engineers validating technical conclusions and authorised roles approving exceptional commitments.

job.title: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing, Technical and Scientific Products
